title: ReadinessSnapshot
description: Hierarchical readiness projection (Technical Specification SS44, SS51): Provider -> Capability -> Product -> Estate -> Tenant. Readiness SHALL be explainable -- never merely `ready: false` where structured reasons are available (SS44) -- so every non-READY snapshot carries blocking_reasons drawn from the reason-code registry: the capability_resolution_denial code CapabilityResolution uses where one names the condition, and otherwise a provisioning_blocker code, the vocabulary TenantProvisioning.blocking_reasons also uses.

level.description: Which level of the readiness hierarchy this snapshot reports on.

object_reference.description: The specific object this snapshot is about at its level, e.g. a capability_key when level=CAPABILITY, a product_id when level=PRODUCT, an estate_id when level=ESTATE. Omitted when level=TENANT, since the tenant is already identified by tenant_id.

code.description: A capability_resolution_denial or provisioning_blocker code from contracts/authorization/v1/reason-code-registry.yaml, e.g. BINDING_NOT_FOUND (matches the Technical Specification SS51 example verbatim), or a release_drift code whose readiness_effect in topology/v1 release-policy.yaml is BLOCKED (ADR-BCP-025 section 2.8). A release_drift code is a readiness consequence, never a capability resolution denial.

degrading_reasons.description: Why a snapshot is DEGRADED: release_drift codes that degrade it without blocking it (ADR-BCP-025 section 2.8): a drift whose readiness_effect in topology/v1 release-policy.yaml is DEGRADED, or a BLOCKED-effect drift on a dependency that is not mandatory or still has a usable binding on an unaffected instance. Visible, never blockers.

contributing_snapshots.description: Snapshots at the level below that this one aggregates, e.g. a PRODUCT snapshot referencing the CAPABILITY snapshots of its mandatory capabilities. A snapshot's own status SHALL be derivable from these plus its own direct checks -- never asserted independently of them.
